A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain complete, readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The formatting changes do not impede reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimizer experiments on regression, Poisson PINNs, modular arithmetic, and MNIST, including appendix experiments and repeated-seed results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, their training and evaluation results, and the supplementary experiments and seed replications in the appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix B retain the same GN, LM, and generalized Gauss-Newton procedures, including continuation with Adam or AdamW. No algorithmic component, architecture, or training objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same one- and two-dimensional regression problems, Poisson PINNs, polynomial regression, MLP and transformer modular arithmetic, and MNIST experiments with MSE and cross-entropy losses.

E2.justification: The comparator sets match within corresponding experiments. For example, Figure 4 retains SGD, Adam, and LM; Figure 8 retains Adam and GGN; and Appendix C retains the Adam, SGD, and GGN comparison.

E3.justification: Tables 1–7 retain the same model dimensions, sample counts, training fractions, learning rates, batch sizes, and solver settings. Evaluation metrics, damping schedules, and optimizer-switch points are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The scaling studies, frequency-error analyses, MNIST cross-entropy analysis in Appendix C, and transformer continuation experiment in Appendix D are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Appendix E and Figure 13 already report five additional seeds, median curves, and shaded minimum-to-maximum ranges in v1. v2 preserves the same run-count information and uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The result plots and accompanying numerical and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Figure 8 still reports approximately 45% final validation accuracy for GGN versus 100% for Adam.

T1.justification: Lemmas 3.1–3.3, the mathematical assumptions and derivations, and the SVD-based proofs in Appendix A are unchanged. Equation movement and typesetting do not alter their content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about mitigating spectral bias, shortening grokking delays, and recovering generalization through subsequent first-order optimization.

C2.justification: The NTK-to-rich-regime interpretation and limitations concerning PGD generalization and train/test dataset sizes remain unchanged. Appendix D retains the qualification that transformer continuation can require a comparable number of iterations to ordinary Adam.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Reproducibility Statement promising experiment and figure scripts through Sandia's GitHub organization after internal information review. This supplies a conditional code-release plan absent from v1; it does not establish that code is already available or add implementation settings beyond the existing appendix.

R1.justification: The cited works and scientific positioning relative to prior NTK, spectral-bias, grokking, and optimization research are unchanged. Citation punctuation and reference reflow are presentation changes.

P1.justification: v2 adds the short Reproducibility Statement, expands funding acknowledgments, and replaces the preprint status with ICLR 2026 publication text. Scientific prose and section organization remain essentially unchanged, with updated heading and citation styles.

P2.justification: v2 adopts conference headers and title styling, resizes some figures, and changes their placement; for example, Figure 2 is smaller, and Figures 5 and 7 move to earlier pages. All 13 figures and seven tables remain, with unchanged scientific content and table structures.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument, experimental evidence, proofs, and implementation settings remain unchanged. The new reproducibility statement clarifies a future release plan but supplies neither a released codebase nor additional replication instructions. Together with the funding disclosures and formatting adjustments, this does not establish a meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
